title: Strang: acts not evil in themselves are all decreed, some absolutely, some respectively
source_text: VIII. Quod spectat autem actus quibus natura sua malitia annexa non est, vult eos omnes dici posse a Deo decretos atque praedefinitos, sed rursus non omnes eadem ratione. Alios enim, juxta ipsum, Deus absolute decrevit, alios autem respective. Intelligit autem illa absolute a Deo decerni & praedefiniri, quae ante considerationem voluntatis nostrae decrevit, imo ad quae statuit voluntatem nostram praedeterminare. Respective vero, quae Deus decrevit fore secundum liberam nostram electionem, in iis in quibus liberam nobis optionem concedit, ita ut licitum sit hoc vel illud eligere.
pass_a_gloss: VIII. But as regards acts to which malice is not annexed by their nature, he wills that they all can be said to be decreed and predefined by God, but again not all in the same way. For some, according to him, God decreed absolutely, but others respectively. He understands those to be decreed and predefined by God absolutely, which he decreed before the consideration of our will, nay to which he determined to predetermine our will. But respectively, those which God decreed to be according to our free election, in those in which he grants us free option, so that it is lawful to choose this or that.
pass_b_english: As for acts that are not by their nature joined to malice, he holds that all of them can be said to be decreed and predefined by God, but again not all in the same way. Some, on his view, God decreed absolutely, others respectively.

By 'absolutely' decreed and predefined he means those that God decreed before considering our will, indeed those to which he resolved to predetermine our will. By 'respectively' he means those that God decreed would come about according to our free choice, in matters where he grants us a free option, so that we may lawfully choose this or that.

lemmas.latin: quibus natura sua malitia annexa non est
lemmas.gloss: to which malice is not annexed by their nature

lemmas.latin: ita ut licitum sit hoc vel illud eligere
lemmas.gloss: so that it is lawful to choose this or that

choices.why: Strang's term for acts decreed with regard to the will's foreseen free choice, as opposed to 'absolutely'; kept as his technical adverb.
